notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Prepared detailed implementation plan at 6c74cf8a2554c08a2e242b947dcfc6a672749e46. See NOTE-20260908-mcp-runtime-operations-plan. Source inspection confirmed session-map-only requireClaim, generic authorization permitting absent reservations, ProcessManager.start rejecting an existing owned group, synchronous release/renew outside lifecycle, and capacity retention after unconfirmed cleanup. Plan adds strict claimed-operation validation, no-op start, bounded restart deduplication, release ordering and safe response/audit handling. No feature implementation or runtime reproduction was performed; status open and priority next retained.

problem: MCP can currently start or switch a server only as a side effect of claim_project. Repeating a claim for an already running server is a no-op, and release_project_claim intentionally leaves the server running, so an agent cannot explicitly restart or stop the runtime it owns.

risk.rollback: Remove the explicit MCP runtime tools while retaining the existing read, claim, renew, and release contract. Existing claims and managed processes must remain unchanged.

scope: Add start_project, restart_project, and stop_project MCP tools over the existing serialized ControlService runtime operations; do not expose arbitrary commands, ports, or filesystem paths.

Require the calling MCP session to hold the active agent claim for the target project. Resolve the lease token only from private session state and reject unclaimed projects, another owner's claim, stale claims, and mismatched project or reservation identifiers.

Start and restart only the worktree pinned by the active claim. Starting an already running claimed worktree is idempotent; restarting performs a controlled stop and start even when placement is unchanged; stopping leaves the claim held and releases its server-capacity slot.

Apply the existing global server-capacity gate to starts and restarts and preserve one slot across the stop/start gap. Release pending capacity exactly once; after failed launch or stop, actual owned processes keep their slot until cleanup is confirmed.

Return the resulting runtime snapshot and explicit operation error without exposing MCP credentials, lease secrets, session identifiers, command arrays, or unbounded logs. Attribute every operation and failure to the MCP agent identity in the audit and controller logs.

Update the packaged Worktree Switcher skill so agents inspect status before acting, use explicit restart or stop only when the task authorizes disruption, verify placement and phase afterward, and understand that releasing a claim still does not stop the server.

Read notes/NOTE-20260908-mcp-runtime-operations-plan/implementation-plan.md before implementation. It specifies proposed strict input/result contracts, action-state behavior, claim expiry checks, response safety, integration and delivery sequence.

Validate the exact persisted active agent reservation, owner and private lease token after lifecycle lock entry and before new spawn. The existing generic reservation policy allows unclaimed projects and is insufficient for these tools; preserve generic HTTP/local-user behavior.

Add bounded session-scoped deduplication using required idempotency keys so response loss cannot trigger a second restart. Proposed limits are 64 accepted entries per session and 512 globally, with no eviction/re-execution within the session lifetime and rejection before mutation when full.

Serialize explicit claim release with runtime transitions while keeping atomic automatic renewal timely. Cancel unstarted requests on session close, own in-flight cleanup to completion, and drain before closing Git/persistence/logging.

Use a compact allowlisted operation receipt and safe correlated actor reference. Preserve actual runtime, leaseHeld and capacity on failure without a full post-operation Git snapshot or exposing session IDs, secret values and arbitrary errors.
title: Control managed server runtime through MCP
validation: Claim a stopped project and verify start_project starts only the claimed worktree; repeat start_project and verify it is idempotent without spawning a second process.
Restart a running claimed project and verify exactly one controlled stop/start cycle, stable port and worktree placement, retained claim ownership, and no transient second capacity slot.

Stop a running claimed project and verify its complete owned process tree exits, its capacity slot is released, the claim remains active, and release_project_claim still does not affect runtime state.

Verify every runtime tool rejects a project without this session's active claim, another owner's reservation, a stale or mismatched reservation, malformed identifiers, and attempts to target an arbitrary worktree or command.

Run concurrent MCP and HTTP operations for one project and verify existing per-project serialization, reservation authorization, capacity accounting, audit attribution, and failure isolation remain correct.
Verify MCP responses, errors, audit records, and logs never expose bearer tokens, lease secrets, session identifiers, or secret environment values.

Cover the stale session-claim map and generic authorization null-reservation case, exact reservation replacement, and expiry after delayed Git/stop/port checks. An active claim must be revalidated before a new spawn.

Cover same-key concurrent/delayed retries, conflicting key reuse, separate deliberate restart keys and ledger saturation. Accepted keys execute at most once in their documented session scope; replay receipts are timestamped rather than presented as current state.

Cover disconnect/cancellation before mutation, during stop/start and after completion, session closure, queued release, automatic renewal and controller shutdown. No late spawn, abandoned cleanup, premature capacity release or unobserved timer rejection.

Use a claimed-but-stopped fixture produced by claim then stop; verify start no-op behavior, restart at full capacity, failed-start residual ownership and stop of an owned process whose worktree disappeared. Preserve unrelated port listeners and same-project cache/test coordination.

Run focused runtime/lifecycle/MCP/process/store tests, pnpm check and pnpm build, plus affected dashboard verification when shared runtime changes alter UI behavior. Record actual isolated process-tree evidence before closing the item.
value: An agent that owns a project can deliberately recover, restart, or shut down its managed development server without bypassing Worktree Switcher or disturbing another owner.
